comments.text: MQ map strip: 64 cells, one per world column, read indexed from $0600 by the resident at $099D, $3518, $355F, $3B54 (in $3B51), $418A (in $4173), $4C36, $4C5F, $4CA7, $4CB2, $4F77, $4F93, $4FD8 and $502E (the position mask $5E is $FF here, from $59A1 indexed by header byte $0705 = 0; the map is read as far as column 255, so the cells at $0640-$06FF count too). The low nibble of a cell selects its block type through the table at $073E. Columns 0 to 63 hold 00 01 02 03 and then $04 in every cell from column 4; the 192 bytes after the strip ($0640-$06FF) are $04 too.

192 bytes ($0640-$06FF) after the 64-cell strip, all $04 (the same value as the last cell of the strip). The position mask $5E is $FF in this scene ($59A1 indexed by header byte $0705 = 0), so columns 64 to 255 reach these bytes; whether the scene's bounds keep the player inside the first 64 columns was not checked.

Start of the 32-byte scene header that the loader at $557A unpacks after the map. The bytes are $50 51 2D 2D 00 00 00 00 0C 0A 0E 0E 0E 0E 55 51. The loader reads $0701 ($51, "Q") as the name character of the picture P and character set C resources it loads to $BC00 and $E000, $070F ($51, "Q") as the name character of the overlay U loaded to $8B00, and $0703 ($2D, "-") as the extra costume selector, where a dash means none. $0700 and $0702 are not read by the loader.

Three numeric header bytes: $0704 (0) is the loop limit the loader compares at $568F and is read by the camera and motion routines ($287C, $3447, $4409, $48C6); the resident also stores to it at $6B9E. $0705 (0) indexes the tables at $59A1 and $59A8 that set $5E, $5F and $60, and from $566A $0706 (0) is shifted right twice into $02C8, its low two bits going to bits 7-6 of $02C7.

Seven colour bytes ($0707-$070D = 00 0C 0A 0E 0E 0E 0E) read by $5A34: $0708 and $0709 go to the VIC background colour registers $D022 and $D023, $0707 is cached at $02DD as the display colour, and $070A-$070D are copied to the four message palette bytes $6998-$699B unless $0387 and $26 are both negative ($5A46-$5A4D then skip to $5A6D).
Two bytes, "UQ" ($55 $51): the overlay resource name, whose second character the loader compares with its cache at $508E and loads at $8B00 ($070F).

Ten bytes ($0710-$0719 = 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00): depth thresholds. The table is read indexed from $0710 by the object grid and placement routines at $28CA, $37B9 (in $37B4), $383F, $3863 and $5487; $0711 is read at $548A, $0718 at $5397 and $0719 at $53B9.

Costume selector ($0D), read at $51EA and copied to $02C5 (replaced by 4 when $0385 is non-negative and $0565 is negative); it indexes the initial-animation table at $5985, read at $520D. The three bytes after it ($071B-$071D = FF 02 FF) are read at $5201, $5207 and $51E4 when entry placement starts.
Sixteen replacement cell nibbles for OPEN, indexed by the current cell's low nibble. Bytes: 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0A 0B 0C 0D 0E 0F. Nibbles that change: none.
Sixteen replacement cell nibbles for CLOSE, indexed by the current cell's low nibble. Bytes: 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0A 0B 0C 0D 0E 0F. Nibbles that change: none.

Sixteen low-nibble-to-type values read indexed by the resident at $351E, $3565, $3B5A (in $3B51), $4192 (in $4173), $4A8E, $4B27, $4F7D, $4F99, $4FE8 and $503E (bytes: 00 00 00 00 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 01 01). Sixteen inclusive upper column bounds read by $4115 (bytes: FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF FF). Resident $411C takes the first entry whose bound is at least the coarse column, so each region is the span of columns up to its bound.

Sixteen zero bytes ($075E-$076D) between the column thresholds and the selectors. The scan at $411C reads at most index 14 ($075C), so it reads none of them. The resident uses $075E,X/Y as per-cell state for special map cells: $381C increments the counter of the cell just entered, and $38FE (update_grid_special_cell) reads and writes it at $3901 and $3915, with Y the low nibble of a special map cell.

Sixteen source selectors, one per region (bytes: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00). Resident $412B reads the one for the region found at $411C: 0 uses the region itself as the table index (bank 0), 1 takes bits $60 of the state byte $0500, 2 takes bits $60 of $0501, and 3 or more take bits $60 of the shared PRNG. Pairs 0 to 8 of the [verb,object] list scanned by resident dispatch_wheel_command ($5F43) over offsets $00-$BE, two dictionary indices each; a zero is a wildcard, so a verb's specific objects come before its [verb,0] fallback, and the first negative byte ends the scan. The handler for the pair at $8B00+2n is the word at $8BC0+2n. This stretch: DO YOU HAVE elephants over me; DO YOU HAVE power over me; DO YOU HAVE towels over me; THROW SOME elephants over me; THROW SOME power over me; THROW SOME towels over me; YOU HAVE NO elephants over me; YOU HAVE NO power over me; YOU HAVE NO towels over me.
Negative terminator $FF,$00 of the pair list at $8B12, then $FF,$00 filler pairs to $8BBF that the scan never reaches.

Handler words for pairs 0 to 8 (word n answers the pair at $8B00+2n). A word with a high byte of $80 or more is code the dispatcher jumps to; a smaller high byte is a message, shown as the headered text at the word plus $8000. In order: 0 code $8DD2; 1 code $8DDD; 2 code $8DED; 3 code $8E00; 4 code $8E10; 5 code $8E1E; 6 code $8E2E; 7 code $8DC2; 8 code $8E3E.
174 zero bytes between the handler word table and the stream pointer table at $8C80. The dispatcher scans only pair offsets $00-$BE and nothing in the overlay refers to these bytes.
Three stream pointers read by resident $6B63 as the word at $8C80+2*$0343 (room text modes 0, 1 and 2). All three are zero here: this overlay supplies no run-length stream.
First of five hook entries at the start of the overlay: jmp $8D94, a bare rts, so this hook does nothing in scene 26.
Second hook entry: jmp $8D94 (rts), same as the first.
Third hook entry: jmp $8D94 (rts), same as the first two.
Fourth hook entry: jmp $8C99, the per-frame scene update s26_scene_update (the same slot that holds the update in scene 25).
Fifth hook entry: jmp $8C98, an rts, so this hook does nothing in scene 26.

Sixth entry in the stub block: jmp $8F24, s26_install_descriptor. The resident calls it by jsr at $5DBD; it is not one of the five hooks. $8F24 is also called directly from the two endings ($8E7C, $8EF2).
Shared rts of the fifth hook entry ($8C92).

Per-frame scene update, reached from the fourth hook stub ($8C8F). First runs s26_init ($8DA1, one-time setup), then s26_ambient_sound ($9010). Then handles the edge: if the fall countdown $8DA0 is negative (idle) it runs s26_edge_check ($8EAB); otherwise the player is falling: at count 8 it queues sound $0D, it nudges the player position $0538 by one each frame and counts $8DA0 down; below zero it jumps to s26_fall_ending ($8EDA). After that it plays the opening text once, steps the idle animation, the elephant countdown and the countdown that follows each command (s26_command_countdown $8CF6).

Falling: moves the player position $0538 one step (decrement if it is positive, increment if negative), then counts the fall countdown $8DA0 down. Negative means the fall is over and control goes to s26_fall_ending ($8EDA); otherwise it carries on at $8CC9.
Not falling: calls s26_edge_check ($8EAB), which starts a fall if the player stands outside the safe range.

If the opening-text flag $8D96 is negative, makes it 0 so this runs once, sets the idle animation counter $8D9D to $26 and shows the master text at $902E (decoded: 'I am still your master and you must remain with me until the end of time.') through s26_show_text ($9029). The flag is set to $FF again by s26_ending_alt.

While the idle animation counter $8D9D is non-negative: sets the animation value $034F to 1, counts $8D9D down and, when it passes zero, sets $034F to 0. This gives a short burst of animation after the opening text. A command handler sets $8D9D to $FF to stop it.
If the elephant countdown $8D9B is non-negative, runs s26_elephant_countdown ($8EF6) each frame.

Countdown that follows a command (set to $15 by s26_start_reply). Negative means no command pending and the routine returns. Otherwise it decrements it; reaching 0 goes to s26_win_ending ($8E5F). Y holds the old value and drives the steps below.
When the old count was $13: loads $0246 with the handler's value from $8D9E, increments $63 and queues the sound number saved in $8D99 with $081E (jmp). For other counts above $13 nothing happens.

Counts below $13: if the move flag $8D97 is non-negative, $0246 and $63 are incremented each frame. If $8D98 is non-negative it toggles between 0 and 1 and stores 1, or 3 when the toggle is 0, into $036F, clearing $034F. If $8D9C is non-negative it toggles too: at 1 it writes 4 to $036D/$036E and 2 to $036F, at 0 it writes 0 to $036D/$036E; either way it clears $034F. These drive the sprite poses of the towels and throw replies; their roles are not confirmed.
At old count $11 sets $035F to 3. Below $0B, if $034F is 5 to 7, asks the random generator ($0821) and sets $034F to 7 (three times in four) or 5. At old count $0A sets $035F to 2. Then returns.
Target of the first three hook stubs: a bare rts.
Set-up flag. Negative means s26_init has not run yet; s26_init clears it to 0 so the set-up happens once. It is 0 in the saved game state, so the init is already done there.
Negative means the opening master text is still to be shown (see $8CC9); then incremented to 0. Set to $FF again by s26_ending_alt (the loop at $8EA0-$8EA8).
Set to 3 by the THROW SOME power handler ($8E10); when non-negative, $0246 and $63 are incremented every frame of the command countdown. $FF means off.
Pose toggle used in s26_command_tick_below_13. The YOU HAVE NO towels handler ($8E3E) sets it to 0. $FF means off.
Sound number saved by s26_start_reply ($1C, $2B or $01) and queued with $081E when the command countdown passes $13.
Countdown that starts at $15 when a command handler has run. Negative = idle. At 0 the ending starts (s26_win_ending).
Countdown set to $0A by the YOU HAVE NO elephants handler ($8E2E); run by s26_elephant_countdown. $FF = idle.

Second pose toggle, set to 1 by the DO YOU HAVE towels handler ($8DED) and flipped on each frame of the command countdown once the old count is below $13. $FF = off; s26_ending_alt sets it to $FF again.
Idle animation counter: set to $26 by the opening text, to $FF by s26_start_reply. Initial value $1C in the saved state.

Value written to $0246 when the command countdown passes $13. Five handlers set it, to 1 (YOU HAVE NO power, DO YOU HAVE towels, THROW SOME elephants, THROW SOME towels) or 5 (DO YOU HAVE power); the other four leave the previous value. Initial value 7.

Tested by s26_win_ending ($8E6A). Zero or positive: play the win ending and finish the scene ($0580=2). Negative: the alternate branch s26_ending_alt. Nothing in $8C86-$902B writes it; it is 0 in the saved state.
Fall countdown. $FF = standing safely; set to 9 by s26_edge_check when the player is out of range, then decremented each frame.

One-time scene set-up, called from s26_scene_update ($8C99). If the flag $8D95 is non-negative it returns. Otherwise clears it, installs the command-availability list at $914D with $0833 (X=$4D, Y=$91) and, when $052C is non-zero, writes $10 to $90E8 (a byte inside the congratulations text). Finally enables all eight sprites with $D015=$FF.
